P1:
CFO importer paying yuan, ruble loans.
1. IF ruble is strengthening or expected to (oil/FX inflows up, CBR hawkish, sanctions easing) THEN buy yuan now / accelerate purchases and hedge less; a stronger ruble makes yuan cheaper. CHECK: do not buy yuan when ruble is weakening unless hedging forward.
2. IF ruble weakening or volatile (falling export revenue, rate cuts, new sanctions, capital outflow) THEN buy 30-60% of 1-3 month yuan needs now or lock forwards/NDF-like swaps via bank. CHECK: weaker ruble = costlier yuan, so waiting hurts.
3. IF key rate expected to fall (inflation cooling, dovish CBR signals) THEN prefer floating-rate or short tenor loans (3-6m), avoid long fixed, delay refinancing. CHECK: do not fix at a peak.
4. IF key rate expected to rise or stay high longer THEN fix part (30-50%) of debt, extend tenor, draw credit lines early. CHECK: direction of rate expectation, not current level.
5. IF CBR meeting within 1-2 weeks THEN avoid committing to long fixed terms before it unless signals clear.
6. IF payment-channel problems (bank sanctions, secondary-sanction threats, correspondent delays) THEN diversify to 2-3 banks/channels, prepay earlier, add 2-4 weeks settlement buffer, keep yuan cash buffer. CHECK: lead time 1-3 weeks.
7. IF tariffs, customs or VAT/duty changes on electronics THEN revise landed-cost budget and pricing guidance (pass through 50-100%), pull forward imports before a hike, defer before a cut.
8. IF weak consumer demand/retail slowdown THEN cut purchase budget, raise cash buffer, tighten inventory; IF marketplace commission/rule changes THEN adjust pricing and margin guidance.
9. IF demand peak season (sales events) approaching THEN pre-buy 4-8 weeks ahead; shipping from China takes weeks.
10. IF yuan itself moves (PBoC, CNY vs USD) THEN adjust hedge ratio; yuan appreciation vs ruble is the cost driver.
11. CHECK always: cost impact in rubles = yuan price x CNY/RUB; both legs matter.
Cross-signal patterns: (a) weakening ruble + rate hike expectation + payment friction = strongest: pre-buy and hedge 60%+, fix debt, build buffer. (b) strengthening ruble + falling rates = buy yuan now, stay floating, defer fixing. (c) tariff hike + weak demand = cut volumes, pass through selectively, preserve cash. (d) sanctions on banks + high rates = secure alternative channel and committed credit lines first.
P2:
Head of Procurement, pasta/bakery producer with exports.
1. IF wheat/durum prices rising (poor harvest, export curbs, weather, strong demand) THEN forward-buy 2-4 months of durum/flour now, lock fixed-price contracts, widen supplier base. CHECK: rising prices favor buying early, not waiting.
2. IF prices falling (bumper harvest, export quota increases, ruble weakening making grain exports attractive is the exception) THEN keep spot/short contracts, cut buffer to 3-4 weeks, delay forwards. CHECK: do not lock at highs.
3. IF export duty or quota on grain changes THEN domestic prices typically fall when duty rises (more stays home) and rise when it is removed; adjust forwards accordingly.
4. IF packaging film/polymer or energy prices spike THEN lock 3-6 month supply, add alternate supplier, adjust inventory 2-4 weeks; check surcharges and indexation clauses.
5. IF rail/border/route disruption on Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan or China routes (congestion, closures, tariffs, wagon shortage) THEN reroute or switch carrier, truck for urgent small lots, book rail slots 2-4 weeks ahead, pre-ship ahead of closures. CHECK: lead times of rail 1-3 weeks.
6. IF export destination changes rules (phytosanitary, EAEU certification, import duty) THEN verify documentation first, delay shipments until compliant; temporary vs permanent matters.
7. IF ruble weakens THEN exports more profitable, imported inputs costlier: buy imported packaging earlier. IF ruble strengthens THEN reverse.
8. IF fuel/transport cost up THEN renegotiate freight, consolidate loads, add fuel surcharge clauses.
9. IF supplier disruption/bankruptcy/quality news THEN activate backup, raise safety stock 1-3 weeks.
10. IF demand surge in a destination THEN raise export shipment plan 1-2 months ahead.
11. CHECK: stock buffer in weeks, not tonnes; storage cost vs price risk.
Cross-signal patterns: (a) poor harvest + export curbs lifted + weak ruble = strongest buy signal: forward 4-6 months, diversify. (b) route disruption + peak season = pre-ship and reroute immediately. (c) energy spike + packaging shortage = lock packaging and trim promotions. (d) bumper harvest + export duty rise = stay spot, push for lower prices.
P3:
General Counsel, Russian e-commerce marketplace.
1. IF new or amended law on marketplaces/platform-seller relations (draft stage) THEN engage regulators and industry associations, submit comments, prepare contract amendments; wait for adoption before final changes. CHECK: draft vs enacted, and effective date, often 3-12 months.
2. IF law enacted with effective date THEN set compliance project, update seller/customer contracts and platform rules 30-60 days before effect, train staff.
3. IF personal data rules tighten (localization, consent, breach notification, fines, Roskomnadzor activity) THEN audit data flows, update consent forms and privacy policy, strengthen localization, prepare breach protocol (24-72h reporting). CHECK: Russian regime governs; EU GDPR only for EU data subjects.
4. IF advertising law changes (labeling, restrictions, influencer rules) THEN update ad review process, labeling and seller guidelines immediately; fines apply from effective date.
5. IF antimonopoly (FAS) action or platform dominance proposals THEN review pricing/ranking/commission practices, prepare defense, consider lobbying position.
6. IF consumer protection or marking/traceability requirements (mandatory labeling systems) THEN phase in seller obligations, update contracts; temporary vs permanent measures differ.
7. IF court decision or precedent on liability for counterfeits, seller content or returns THEN revise terms, notice-and-takedown policy, litigation strategy (settle vs contest).
8. IF competitor platform dispute or sellers' complaints rise THEN review contract fairness, reduce litigation risk through amendments.
9. IF sanctions or foreign-law developments affect partners/payments THEN assess contract clauses (force majeure, governing law).
10. IF tax change on marketplaces (VAT, self-employed sellers reporting) THEN update data-sharing and withholding procedures.
11. CHECK: choose lever by stage: monitor, comment, prepare, implement.
Cross-signal patterns: (a) enacted data law + regulator inspections = accelerate audit and remediation now. (b) platform law draft + industry lobbying window = file position and join association before readings. (c) ad rules + marking requirements = unified seller compliance rollout. (d) antimonopoly probe + competitor complaints = freeze contentious term changes, prepare documentation.
P4:
CISO, German regional bank, KRITIS.
1. IF actively exploited vulnerability (CISA KEV, vendor emergency advisory) in software we run THEN patch internet-facing within 24-72h, others within 7 days, apply mitigations immediately. CHECK: exploited and exposed outranks CVSS score alone.
2. IF critical vulnerability without exploitation THEN standard patch cycle 14-30 days, monitor; do not raise alert level.
3. IF ransomware/DDoS campaign targeting banks or financial sector THEN raise alert level, verify offline backups, DDoS protection, restore test, brief SOC 24x7.
4. IF supplier/cloud/software supply-chain compromise THEN inventory exposure, request vendor attestation within 24-48h, isolate integrations, review contracts. DORA third-party register applies.
5. IF regulatory change (DORA, NIS2, BSI KRITIS-Dachgesetz, BaFin guidance) THEN gap analysis, update incident reporting (DORA: initial notice within 4h of classification, 24h of detection), plan by effective date. CHECK: EU/German regime governs; US rules are informational only.
6. IF phishing/social engineering or deepfake fraud wave THEN targeted awareness, simulated phishing, payment callback procedures.
7. IF generative AI tool risk (data leaks, new tools, prompt injection) THEN update AI policy: approved tools list, block unapproved, no customer data in public models.
8. IF geopolitical tension raising state-actor threat THEN heighten monitoring, threat-intel sharing, tabletop exercise within 2-4 weeks.
9. IF breach at peer bank THEN check same indicators of compromise, test incident response.
10. IF zero-day with no patch THEN virtual patching, WAF rules, disable feature, heightened logging.
11. IF end-of-life software news THEN schedule migration, compensating controls.
12. CHECK: tie action to our actual exposure; avoid raising alert for irrelevant generic news.
Cross-signal patterns: (a) exploited vuln + our product + internet exposure = emergency change, alert raised, hunt for compromise. (b) sector ransomware + vendor compromise = vendor isolation plus backup test. (c) new regulation + recent incident at peer = accelerate board-level reporting. (d) phishing wave + AI-deepfake news = payment verification and training.
P5:
COO, Kazakhstan freight forwarder (China-Kazakhstan-Russia, Middle Corridor).
1. IF border/terminal congestion or closure on a route (Khorgos, Altynkol, Dostyk, Brest-type crossings) THEN shift volume to alternative crossings or Middle Corridor, pre-book wagons 2-3 weeks ahead, add transit time and surcharge. CHECK: temporary congestion vs permanent change.
2. IF Middle Corridor/Caspian news (port capacity, ferry schedules, Georgian/Azerbaijani infrastructure) improves THEN raise capacity bookings there; deteriorates THEN keep northern route, add buffer. Caspian lead times 2-4 weeks.
3. IF EU sanctions packages (dual-use, listed entities, transit bans on Russia) THEN tighten cargo and client screening before acceptance, reject or hold flagged HS codes, document end-use. CHECK: EU, US (secondary sanctions) and Kazakh/EAEU regimes differ; strictest applicable governs.
4. IF US secondary sanctions risk on banks THEN verify payment channels, prefer prepayment, reduce Russia-bound exposure.
5. IF fuel price rising THEN renegotiate carrier contracts, add fuel surcharge in pricing; falling THEN lock longer fuel contracts.
6. IF rail tariff changes or wagon shortage THEN reprice, shift to trucks for urgent cargo, lock wagon fleet contracts.
7. IF demand surge (peak season, e-commerce) THEN secure capacity 4-6 weeks ahead, raise prices; IF demand slump THEN consolidate loads, trim carrier commitments.
8. IF EU-China or Russia-bound customs rule change THEN update documentation, inform clients, delay shipments until compliant.
9. IF tenge weakens THEN adjust USD-denominated pricing and costs.
10. IF security/weather/strike disruption THEN activate contingency routes, notify clients.
11. CHECK: pricing direction: raise when capacity scarce or costs up.
Cross-signal patterns: (a) EU sanctions tightening + bank pressure = strict screening and prepayment, drop risky clients. (b) northern route disruption + Middle Corridor improvement = reroute decisively. (c) peak season + wagon shortage = lock capacity early, surcharge. (d) fuel spike + tariff rise = reprice services across all contracts.
P6:
Head of HR and Corporate Security, French retail chain, 140 stores.
1. IF national or Paris-region strikes/transport disruption announced THEN adjust staff schedules, allow remote or flexible start, arrange staff transport, reduce hours; lead time 2-5 days. CHECK: dates and duration.
2. IF large demonstrations or riots expected in specific cities THEN close or shorten hours for stores near routes (e.g. 1-3 days), board up windows, brief staff; reopen after police clearance. CHECK: close only affected stores, not all 140.
3. IF terror threat level raised (Vigipirate to urgence attentat) THEN reinforce guards at entrances, bag checks, evacuation drills, staff briefings within 24-48h.
4. IF crime wave/shoplifting violence or incident at stores THEN add security staff, panic buttons, staff support, incident reporting.
5. IF travel safety alerts (foreign ministry advisories) THEN restrict or defer staff travel to affected countries, recall as needed.
6. IF labor law, minimum wage (SMIC), or pension reform changes THEN update payroll and contracts per effective date, consult CSE (works council) before collective changes. CHECK: French law requires consultation; changes are permanent vs temporary.
7. IF union action or negotiation (NAO) news THEN open dialogue early, prepare contingency staffing, consider modest raises to prevent strikes.
8. IF heat waves, floods, storms THEN adapt working hours, safety measures, cooling, closure if prefect orders.
9. IF major events (sports, holidays, sales periods) THEN raise staffing and security 1-2 weeks ahead.
10. IF health alerts THEN hygiene measures, sick-leave guidance.
11. IF crisis occurs THEN communicate to employees quickly via SMS and email, clear instructions, updates every few hours.
12. CHECK: safety first over sales; proportional response.
Cross-signal patterns: (a) transport strike + demonstration at city center = close affected stores and reschedule staff. (b) terror threat raised + major event = reinforced security plus staff briefing. (c) pay reform + union mobilization = early dialogue and CSE consultation. (d) riots + prior vandalism = pre-emptive closure of nearby stores and stock protection.
